evals.prompt: whats on my plate today? anything i missed
evals.expected_output: A briefing built from a single `apple-reminders list --incomplete` read, grouped into Overdue / Due today / Upcoming / Unscheduled with empty groups skipped, each item naming its reminder list and using exact dates with weekdays. If the read reported `_warning` / `total_available`, the answer either re-reads with a higher `--limit` or states that the view was truncated.

assertions.text: Ran `apple-reminders list` with `--incomplete` rather than an unfiltered read, so undated inbox items are included
Reminders are grouped by operational meaning (overdue / today / upcoming / unscheduled) rather than dumped as a flat list, and each item names its list

If the response contained `_warning` or `total_available`, the answer re-read with a larger `--limit` or explicitly said the briefing was truncated; it did not claim completeness from a truncated read
No raw JSON is shown to the user

evals.prompt: add pick up prescription to my errands list, friday 6pm
evals.expected_output: A `list` read first to resolve the exact list title, then `create --title "Pick up prescription" --list "<exact title>" --due <YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM>` with the concrete Friday date computed in local time, then a follow-up read to confirm the due date landed. The reply states the resolved date and the list the reminder actually went to.

assertions.text: A read was performed before the write to resolve the exact list title instead of passing the user's wording straight into `--list`
`--due` was passed as an absolute local datetime such as 2026-08-07T18:00, not as 'friday', '+1d', or any relative or natural-language form
The `list` field returned by `create` was checked against the intended list, because an unmatched `--list` silently falls back to the default list
A follow-up read confirmed the due date, since `create` does not echo `due` back
The reply states the concrete date chosen (with weekday) so a misreading of 'friday' would be visible

evals.prompt: move the gym shoes thing to my work list
evals.expected_output: The read shows both a `Work` and a `Workout` list. The answer does not pass `--list work`, because the substring match makes the winner unpredictable. It either passes the exact intended title after determining it from the reminder's content, or names both candidates and asks which one.

assertions.text: Recognized that `--list` matches by case-insensitive substring, so a partial name like 'work' can resolve to the wrong list
Either passed an exact resolved list title or surfaced both candidate lists to the user instead of guessing
The write targeted the reminder by its `id` from a read, not by title

evals.prompt: push the tax filing task to next monday morning
evals.expected_output: The reminder id is resolved from a read, the current due date is captured first, then `update --id <id> --due <YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM>` patches only the due date. The `due` value returned by `update` is compared against the intended value, and the reply reports the change as old -> new.

assertions.text: Only `--due` was passed to `update`; title, list, priority, and notes were not re-sent
'next monday morning' was resolved to a concrete absolute local datetime before building the command
The `due` value in the `update` response was used as the read-back check, since a failed date parse is silently dropped and still returns ok:true
The reply reports the change as old date -> new date with weekdays

evals.prompt: attach this screenshot to my visa reminder and tag it #urgent
evals.expected_output: A plain statement that the on-device `apple-reminders` command exposes no attachment support and no tags, with the closest honest alternative offered (referencing the file path in `--notes`, or a priority instead of a tag) and the note that a real attachment or tag has to be added by hand in the Reminders app. No fabricated success.

assertions.text: States plainly that attachments and tags are not available through this command
Does not report success for attaching a file or adding a tag, and does not silently write a tag into `--notes` as a substitute without saying so
Offers a concrete alternative and identifies the Reminders app as the way to get a real attachment or tag

evals.prompt: clear out everything in my shopping list thats already done
evals.expected_output: The ambiguity between completing and deleting is resolved before writing. The qualifying set is enumerated from a bounded `list --completed --list "<exact title>"` read first. If deletion is intended, `title`, `list`, `due`, `priority`, and `notes` are captured beforehand and reported so each item could be recreated; the batch stops and reports partial progress if any single write returns ok:false.

assertions.text: The qualifying reminders were enumerated from a bounded read before the first write, not deleted by applying a filter blindly
The difference between `complete` (reversible via --undo) and `delete` (irreversible on this path) was addressed rather than assumed
If deleting, the pre-delete state of each reminder was captured and reported so it could be recreated by hand; recoverability from Recently Deleted was not promised
The final report lists the exact affected items with their list names, not just a count
A failed write in the middle of the batch would stop the run and be reported, rather than the batch continuing and being reported as complete

evals.prompt: 비자 서류 준비 미리알림 제일 급한 거로 올려줘
evals.expected_output: The skill triggers on a non-English request, resolves the reminder id from a read, and sets `--priority 1` because the EventKit scale is inverted — 1 is the highest priority, not 9 or 10. The reply is written in the user's language and reports the change without exposing the reminder's notes or its raw id.

assertions.text: The skill triggered on a Korean-language request that never uses the word 'reminder' in English
`--priority 1` was used for highest priority; the inverted EventKit scale was respected and no value above 9 was passed
The reminder was targeted by its `id` resolved from a read, and only `--priority` was patched
The reply is in the user's language and does not print the reminder's notes, raw JSON, or the raw id
